_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 4: Magellan / LLAMAS (one preset per arm: blue, green, red)
_meta.companion: data/round4/llamas.md (same content as a Markdown section in the format of data/presets_research.md); same JSON structure as data/presets_sources_3.json. Extra keys: 'recommended_presets_by_arm' (explorer inputs per arm, numbers only) and 'stage' on entries whose source is a design concept. Top-level 'multiplex' holds the objects-per-exposure row.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values (is_derived = the value itself is derived). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (whitespace/glyph-normalised).
_meta.quote_normalisation: Quotes copied from pdftotext (layout and raw) / HTML text / raw repository text files; double primes (rendered '00' in F20), modifier primes, micro/mu, curly quotes, dashes, minus and tilde-operator glyphs normalised; line-end hyphenation joined; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows quoted as whitespace-separated cells; pieces that differ only in punctuation/spacing are accepted.

llamas.title: Magellan / LLAMAS (lenslet-fed fibre IFU: 2400 fibres into eight identical bench spectrographs, each split by dichroics into blue / green / red arms with VPH grisms)
llamas.recommended_preset: Three presets (B, G, R), identical except for the disperser and band. Common: D = 6.5 m, F = 4.0 (collimator focal ratio; the MLA turns the native f/11 into f/4.4 at the fibre and FRD keeps 95.6% inside f/4), 110 um core (0.873" at f/4.0) entered as the slit of equal line width 0.756" (trace width the same), 300 spectra per detector, collimator = Mirror (spherical, on-axis), W = 50 mm (f_col = 200 mm), camera f = 70 mm (f/1.40 on the beam; ETC f/1.28 monochromatic; F20 effective f/1.05), transmission (VPH) grating in first order, detector 2048 x 2048 x 13.5 um (e2v CCD42-40; red deep depletion). VPH line densities and angles are NOT published: use the DERIVED effective values (symmetric Bragg setting at lamC) that put the published coverage on the 2048 px chip -- BLUE: G = 2233 /mm, alpha = beta = 28.13 deg, lamC = 4222 A (3417-4947 A); GREEN: G = 1425 /mm, 24.96 deg, lamC = 5923 A (4634-7100 A); RED: G = 1070 /mm, 26.93 deg, lamC = 8466 A (6771-10000 A). Validate against: coverage (MITSPEC, by construction); R 1500-2500 / 1400-2400 / 1750-2500 (MITSPEC lab), R ~ 2000 (F20, S26), 2200 (ETC); mean dispersion 0.747 / 1.204 / 1.577 A/px and centre dispersion 0.762 / 1.204 / 1.609 A/px from the post-first-light arc table (independent of the coverage used to set G); fibre image 2.85 px (LSF FWHM 2.47 px); trace pitch 6.46 px.

Simcoe et al. 2022, Proc. SPIE 12184, 121840D, 'Construction update on the Magellan LLAMAS integral field spectrograph': SPIE abstract page only; no open copy (not in ADS, NSF PAR or arXiv).

SPIE 2026 paper 14149-57, 'First year into operations of LLAMAS ... design, build and commissioning overview, results and performance': presentation page found, no text retrieved; not on arXiv as of 2026-10-17.

As-built camera prescription and as-built collimator / camera focal lengths: 200 mm and 70 mm come from the 2017 pocket guide (collimator) and the 2024 ETC definition files and F20 (camera), i.e. design values.
A published dispersion (A/px) and sampling (px per FWHM) for the built instrument: both DERIVED here.
On-sky (post-commissioning) resolving power per arm: the MITSPEC ranges are pre-ship laboratory measurements (page last modified 2024-09-14); S26 gives only R ~ 2000.

As-built dichroic crossover wavelengths: MITPROP says 'Basic parameters of the as-built instrument (wavelengths, spectral resolution, dichroic crossover points, etc) are listed at the Specifications page', but that page lists only per-channel coverage (overlaps 4634-4947 A and 6771-7100 A).
Fibre pitch along the pseudo-slit and slit length (DERIVED from the pipeline trace table).

Stenzel 2022 (MIT S.M. thesis, 'Model-Based Verification of The Large Lenslet Array Magellan Spectrograph', DSpace 1721.1/144841) was downloaded and read: its Table 4.1 lists the optical parameters by name only (no values), and it uses R = 2200 like the ETC; not used and not saved.

The old project pages www.mit.edu/~rsimcoe/llamas/instrument.html and index.html now return a 404 page, and the Wayback Machine had no snapshot; search-engine snippets of them (e.g. 'R=2200', per-channel R 1680-2750 / 1500-2410 / 2000-2750, '350-980nm') could not be verified and are not used.
conflicts: Camera focal length: 70 mm (F20 production units; ETC) vs 90 mm (PG17 2017 concept; F20 prototype).

Camera focal ratio: f/1.28 'monochromatic' (ETC) vs 'effective f/1.05, in polychromatic light and across all field positions' (F20) vs F/1.4 (PG17, 90 mm design); 70/50 = f/1.40 on the 50 mm beam (DERIVED).

Dichroic splits: 690 and 475 nm (F20) vs band edges 480 and 690 nm (FR20; ETC) vs one dichroic at 570 nm (PG17 two-arm concept). As built the arms overlap: blue to 4947 A, green from 4634 A; green to 7100 A, red from 6771 A (MITSPEC).
Red band end: 970 nm (FR20; F20 abstract) vs 975 nm (F20 Sec. 2.4; ETC) vs '1 micron' (MITSPEC, MITHOME) vs ~10048 A at pixel 2047 (PYJ, DERIVED).

Blue on-chip range: 3417-4947 A (MITSPEC) vs 3240-4808 A from the post-first-light arc look-up table (PYJ, DERIVED; the fit is anchored by lines 3545.6-4657.9 A, so both ends are extrapolated). Green and red agree within 20-50 A. The derived blue G_eff is 2233 /mm from MITSPEC vs 2215 /mm from the arc fit.
Resolving power: per-arm ranges 1500-2500 / 1400-2400 / 1750-2500 (MITSPEC, lab) vs R = 2000 (F20, FR20, S26) vs R = 2200 (ETC) vs R = 1300 (PG17 concept).
Total passband: 350-970 nm (F20 abstract, FR20) vs 350-975 nm (F20 Sec. 1) vs 3400 A-1 um (MITHOME) vs 3500-9700 A (S26) vs 360-970 nm (PG17).
Fibres: 2400 active of 3200 installed, 300 per slit (F20) vs 2,392 spatial elements, 4 x 300 + 4 x 298 (MITSPEC) vs 2560 total and 320 per spectrograph (PG17).
Field of view: 34" x 35" (MITSPEC) vs 35" x 35" (MITHOME) vs 37" x 37" (F20, FR20, S26) vs 40" x 36" (PG17).
Fibre run: 5 m total (F20) vs ~10 m from focal plane to the spectrograph bank (MITHOME) vs 4.5 m (PG17).
notes: Explorer mapping (DESI convention): D = 6.5 m, F = 4.0 (the spectrograph's own focal ratio, so f_col = F x W = 200 mm comes out right); entrance = slit of equal line width (sqrt3/2) x 0.8727" = 0.756"; the trace width across the dispersion is the same fibre image, so no separate traceW is needed. The real sky sampling is the 0.75" hexagonal lenslet, which images the pupil on the fibre.
Collimator = Mirror (spherical, on-axis; the slit sits inside the collimated beam at its focus, fibres fanned to the Schmidt condition).

Disperser: the explorer models a bare plane VPH. LLAMAS uses VPH grisms (prism on the front plate) at the camera entrance pupil; the derived G_eff and symmetric-Bragg angle reproduce the published coverage on a 70 mm camera but do not describe the true grating, prism or camera angle.

Sanity check of f_cam = 70 mm: with G_eff fixed by the band edges, the model's central dispersion (0.761 / 1.227 / 1.607 A/px) matches the arc-table derivative at pixel 1024 (0.762 / 1.204 / 1.609 A/px), and the arc-table dispersion falls by 21% / 13% / 14% across the blue / green / red chip (model: 19% / 17% / 18%, from cos(beta) at alpha ~ 25-28 deg). The arc data alone cannot separate f_cam from G (degenerate), so 70 mm rests on F20 and the ETC.

Spectra per detector: all 300 (or 298) are IFU science fibres; sky comes from the field itself and calibration light enters through the same fibres from the front-end calibration unit (F20 Sec. 2.1). A 50% sub-array mode (masks in the IFU focal plane) doubles the trace spacing (MITPROP: 'In this occulted mode, the inter-fiber spacing is doubled at the slit for enhanced control of systematics').
Two blue detectors (1A and 4A) were damaged in the 2025-2026 data (S26: 'We dithered to cover gaps left by the two damaged blue detectors (detectors 1A and 4A).').
ETC sensor lines give read noise 2.46 e- (blue, green) and 2.29 e- (red) and dark 0.00119 / 0.00192 e-/s/px; F20 reports 2.3 e- at 75 kHz for the first production heads.
Pipeline wavelength grid limits (PYJ arcLlamas.py): blue 3200-4947, green 4570-7100, red 6570-10038 A -- consistent with the blue chip reaching below 3417 A.
